entries.content:
Vercel Security Review is now in public beta for Pro and Enterprise teams. Once enabled, every push to a connected GitHub repository is automatically reviewed for vulnerabilities, and findings are reported in the Vulnerabilities dashboard.

Copy link to headingWhat triggers a review

Security Review runs automatically when code is pushed to a connected GitHub repository. Because reviews start from push events rather than pull requests, direct and force pushes to your production branch are reviewed as well. Every project affected by a single push is reviewed together.

Copy link to headingWhat a finding includes

Each finding records the project, environment, branch, and commit, with a summary, a suggested fix, and an AI-generated severity rating.

Security Review adds its own GitHub check to each commit it reviews. When there's a pull request, it also posts findings as review comments that link back to each finding. On public repositories, finding details stay in the dashboard.

Copy link to headingFixes and resolution

Clicking Fix with Vercel Agent on a vulnerability report hands the finding to Vercel Agent, which proposes a fix and opens a pull request for you to review. Nothing merges until you approve it.

To fix findings with your coding agent instead, use 

vercel security vulnerabilities
in the Vercel CLI, or copy any finding as Markdown or JSON.

Copy link to headingSecurity policies

Teams can write security policies in plain language, for all projects or specific ones, to give Security Review more context about how they build. Set a team policy in Agent settings and a project policy in the project's Security settings.

Copy link to headingLimitations

Security Review analyzes source code. It isn't a security audit, and it doesn't perform runtime or penetration testing. It helps you find vulnerabilities but doesn't guarantee your application is free of them.

Copy link to headingPricing

Security Review is billed at the Vercel Agent rate: provider inference at the underlying token rate with no markup, plus the Vercel Token Rate of $0.25 per million tokens (input, cached, output). Reviews run on each push to GitHub, so cost scales with how often you push and how much code changes.

Security reviews are free until November 10, 2026, and fixes made with Vercel Agent are billed at the Vercel Agent rate.

Enable Security Review in your team’s Agent settings, or read the documentation and the announcement to learn more. The CLI command needs Vercel CLI 65.10.0 or later.

Contributors

Talha Tariq, Karishma Asthana

entries.content:
Vercel CI can now run on a GitHub repository that has no Vercel project. Until now you had to create an empty project just to connect the repository.

To enable it, you need:

  • The Vercel GitHub App installed with access to the repository

  • Your GitHub account connected to your Vercel account

  • Write or admin permission on the repository

Then, from a clone of the repository, run:

      
vercel ci enable

CI is enabled for the team your CLI is set to. Pass 

--scope
to use a different one. From the next push, tasks run as configured in your repository.

Private GitHub repositories only. Public repositories and other Git providers are not yet supported.

Read the Vercel CI documentation to configure tasks.

entries.title: How Zapier turns ideas into working software in hours with Vercel
entries.summary: Zapier on VercelInteractive partner demos in under two hours with v0, replacing a process that could take weeksFirst versions of three internal applications, each built in one dayA shared daily briefing for more than 60 marketers, replacing individual efforts to assemble the same information3.3 million sandboxes created in one month, isolating the code execution behind Zapier’s AI workloadsBefore
entries.content:
Copy link to headingZapier on Vercel

  • Interactive partner demos in under two hours with v0, replacing a process that could take weeks

  • First versions of three internal applications, each built in one day

  • A shared daily briefing for more than 60 marketers, replacing individual efforts to assemble the same information

  • 3.3 million sandboxes created in one month, isolating the code execution behind Zapier’s AI workloads

Before the industry had a word for agents, Zapier was building them. Today Zapier is the AI orchestration platform connecting AI to the workflows, data, and systems businesses use every day.

Zapier has been a Vercel customer since they began using Vercel for web experiences several years ago. They stayed, and expanded, because every team that needed to ship quickly found the same answer: speed, with the security guardrails already in place. As they grew, so did their adoption of Vercel as more teams found new uses for the platform. Today, Vercel supports work across engineering, partnerships, and marketing, from customer-facing AI to interactive partner demos and internal applications.

The needs vary by team, but the priority is getting useful work into people’s hands quickly. A backend engineer can create an interactive demo of an integration inside a partner’s product. In marketing, a former product marketer with no prior deployment experience can share tools containing sensitive information through a company-approved environment and keep improving them as colleagues use them.

Zapier’s teams are moving faster and doing more than they could before. When the next launch comes around, building on Vercel is a given.

Copy link to headingFrom weeks of prototype work to a demo in under two hours

Every partnership Zapier signs extends what its customers can automate. The Powered by Zapier team is how those partnerships become product, helping SaaS and AI companies embed Zapier’s automation capabilities directly into their own tools, so users can automate without ever leaving the partner’s app. The stakes are high, because Zapier relies on this team to make its platform the entry point to all the software in the world. The problem was speed: collaborating outside the organization took forever, with every prototype requiring screenshots, design time, and frontend resources, and weeks could pass before a partner saw anything clickable.

With v0, the team can create a fully interactive, multi-view prototype in under two hours, showing an embedded Zapier experience inside the partner’s own product.

In two hours using v0, I can now create a fully clickable prototype with 10+ different views. That just wasn’t possible before.Michelle Chu Backend Engineer @ Zapier

Chu’s background is in backend development, not frontend engineering or design, but v0 lets her build these experiences without coordinating a separate design and frontend effort for every partner conversation. Partners can click through the flow and share it with colleagues, using the prototype as a blueprint for implementation alongside the API documentation.

Copy link to headingSharing sensitive internal data securely

In marketing, Joe Stych set out to make the team’s scattered knowledge easier to use. He had spent years in product marketing before becoming a agentic go-to-market engineer, but had never worked out of a Git repository or deployed an application.

At an internal hackathon, he built Marketing Hive, a shared source for positioning, messaging, personas, and competitive intelligence. Sharing his local prototype meant making sensitive information accessible to colleagues without exposing it to everyone else.

“The Hive holds our positioning, personas, and competitive intel, so I couldn't just send people a link. On Vercel it was behind our SSO from the first deploy, so I could share it without exposing it” says Joe Stych, Senior Lead, Agentic GTM at Zapier.

Zapier’s data and security teams had already endorsed Vercel. Stych deployed through the company’s approved internal tooling environment, with access gated behind Zapier’s single sign-on.

He develops in Cursor and keeps code and source material in GitLab, where changes trigger Vercel builds and deployments. If an update needs to be undone, he can roll back the deployment.

The first versions of three of his internal applications took about a day each. In roughly two months, a hackathon project had grown into production software used across marketing. It was built by someone who had never deployed anything before.

Copy link to headingInternal apps for marketing and sales

Marketing Hive holds the knowledge. Marketing OS puts it to work. It gives more than 60 marketers a daily briefing in Slack and a dashboard with what changed across marketing, one update from each team, a win worth celebrating, and progress against goals. Each marketer can start from the briefing instead of assembling the same information from separate channels.

“The first five minutes of your day, you need to look at the Marketing OS update,” says Dan Slagen, Zapier’s CMO.

Readers mark what they found useful, helping Stych prioritize improvements. The briefings also spark discussions in a marketing channel open to everyone at the company.

Stych is building a sales coaching application that brings together account context and industry messaging before a call. Afterward, it reviews the Gong recording to highlight what worked and suggest changes to the talk track.

For the internal applications, he checks reported numbers and the evidence behind claimed insights. Decisions about positioning remain with people, and he says additional safeguards will come before agents publish without human review.

Copy link to headingModel access and isolated code execution

Beyond Marketing OS, a separate team at Zapier uses AI Gateway to send requests to AI models on behalf of customers using Zapier products.

AI Gateway gives us one endpoint for every model provider. When the best model changes, we change with it. No rebuilt integrations, no migration projects.Ryan Anderson Head of Product Marketing @ Zapier

A common endpoint lets an application change or add models without maintaining a separate integration for each provider. Failover gives requests another route when a provider cannot serve them, while unified reporting lets a team see their usage across providers in once place.

Copy link to headingWhat's next

Zapier’s relationship with Vercel began with web experiences and expanded as the company grew, with more teams finding uses for the platform as their needs changed. Today its role spans the software Zapier runs for customers and the tools its people build for one another, and every thread is still widening.

The clearest picture of where it leads is in marketing, where other teams are starting to borrow the pattern. The goal is more versions across the company, and perhaps a Revenue OS for Zapier’s customer-facing teams next, each built the way the first one was, by someone close to the problem. First comes trust. Stych still checks reported numbers and the evidence behind claimed insights, and additional safeguards will come before agents publish without human review.

Across all of it, Vercel helps Zapier put useful work into people’s hands and keep adapting it to the needs of the business.

entries.title: How Mercor ships internal apps and billions of production tokens on one platform
entries.summary: Mercor on VercelBatch jobs cut from 12 hours to 2 hours18M requests and 63B tokens routed through AI Gateway in 10 daysExpert access provisioned in seconds via Vercel PassportOver 2,000 projects created by hundreds of internal buildersMercor connects hundreds of thousands of domain experts with frontier AI labs, helping those labs generate the human data they need to train and evaluate leading mod
entries.content:
Copy link to headingMercor on Vercel

  • Batch jobs cut from 12 hours to 2 hours

  • 18M requests and 63B tokens routed through AI Gateway in 10 days

  • Expert access provisioned in seconds via Vercel Passport

  • Over 2,000 projects created by hundreds of internal builders

Mercor connects hundreds of thousands of domain experts with frontier AI labs, helping those labs generate the human data they need to train and evaluate leading models. It also runs large batches of automated grading jobs to evaluate models for labs and enterprises.

Demand arrives in bursts that can push model traffic to peak capacity for days, even as individual evaluation or labeling jobs carry 24-hour deadlines. With so little time to deliver, requests waiting on a provider’s rate limits can put a client’s deadline at risk.

Mercor’s business teams also need applications tailored to each engagement, giving experts a way to see their tasks and progress without waiting for changes to the core platform.

For Aaron Brown, Mercor’s Head of Security, enabling more people to build means making it easier to give them the access they need and keep track of how they use it. Mercor uses Vercel AI Gateway to manage model access and Vercel Passport to handle secure access to their applications.

Copy link to headingWhen model capacity becomes a customer deadline

Mercor’s mix of direct integrations and third-party gateways could not provide enough token-per-minute capacity for its open-model workloads when demand surged. As requests hit provider limits and entered retry queues, time-sensitive batch jobs stretched beyond 12 hours, consuming more than half of a client’s 24-hour deadline.

AI Gateway provided more inference capacity and failover routing between providers when requests hit rate limits, helping batch work continue instead of waiting in retry queues. Mercor reports that those jobs now finish in 2 to 3 hours, leaving more time to complete the rest of the client’s work. In its first 10 days on Gateway, the team routed 18 million requests and 63 billion tokens, without hitting rate limits.

Mercor continues to use multiple gateways and vendors, valuing Vercel for its combination of model access, controls, and hands-on support when the team needs more capacity. Engineers also get one API for leading foundation model providers and a growing catalog of open models, so they can try a new model without building another provider integration.

Copy link to headingGiving engineers room to experiment within limits

As model use grew, Mercor needed to understand where token spend was going, but its previous setup offered little visibility into usage by team and project. A single loop error in a script could exhaust the available budget.

Hundreds of Mercor engineers now use open models through AI Gateway with per-user keys that carry expiration dates, token limits, and spend limits. Security can give experimentation a budget and an end date, then use the usage records to see which user, project, and workload is driving consumption. Engineers can try different models through the same gateway under those controls, without managing another set of provider credentials each time.

Copy link to headingManaging access as business teams build

A few hundred people across Mercor’s business teams now build applications on Vercel, where the company’s project count has grown from fewer than a dozen to roughly 2,000. Many of those projects are temporary environments for a specific client engagement.

One production use case gives experts detailed views of their project tasks and progress. Rather than ask engineering to add every engagement’s interface to the core platform, business teams build the interfaces themselves and share them with the experts doing the work.

To share those applications, teams need to control who can sign in without taking on a separate authentication setup for every project. Passport provides that common authentication layer, handling sign-in to Vercel deployments through an existing identity provider.

Mercor’s identity team built a product called Audiences, integrating Vercel Passport as a first class primitive, to automate access provisioning. Once a team selects the experts who need access, Audiences creates the IdP group, Vercel connection, and Passport configuration. With that workflow, Mercor reports provisioning access in seconds for audiences ranging from dozens of experts to tens of thousands. Offboarding works the same way in reverse. Because access is derived from the IdP group, removing the group at the end of an engagement removes access to the project, so no stale access is left behind.

Copy link to headingLimiting what each agent can do

Alongside those applications, Mercor uses agents to answer questions from experts in its marketplace, automate HR workflows, and help employees navigate internal systems. Mercor’s approach is to give each agent narrow permissions suited to its job, rather than everything available to the person who invoked it.

For agents that use open models through AI Gateway, Mercor can also scope model access, set expiration dates, and cap spending. That governs their model use while Mercor separately determines which systems and actions each agent can access.

Copy link to headingWhat’s next

Mercor expects more open models to power its internal agents and systems, and more teams outside engineering to build tools for experts. As that work grows, the company wants teams to spend less time setting up model integrations and application authentication so they can respond to client workloads with tight deadlines.

The aim is to make the secure path the fastest path, with shared model access and repeatable authentication workflows helping experts get the tools they need and labs get their work back on time. Mercor wants to support that growth without security work increasing at the same rate.

About Mercor: Mercor is an AI data company that organizes human intelligence for AI training and evaluation. Its network of more than 5M experts, from doctors to lawyers to engineers, powers benchmarks, enterprise evals, RL environments, post-training and agent deployments.

entries.title: How OpenEvidence scales medical search for 650K doctors
entries.summary: OpenEvidence on VercelServes 650,000 doctors with medical searchCompletes production deployments in about five minutesAbsorbs traffic spikes without additional capacity provisioningReduced serverless spend by 90% with Fluid computeUpdates doctor- and patient-facing applications independentlyOpenEvidence helps physicians find medical evidence during care, whether they’re checking a dosage on intens
entries.content:
Copy link to headingOpenEvidence on Vercel

  • Serves 650,000 doctors with medical search

  • Completes production deployments in about five minutes

  • Absorbs traffic spikes without additional capacity provisioning

  • Reduced serverless spend by 90% with Fluid compute

  • Updates doctor- and patient-facing applications independently

OpenEvidence helps physicians find medical evidence during care, whether they’re checking a dosage on intensive care rounds or handling a case outside their specialty without a specialist nearby. Answers draw on peer-reviewed literature and include citations, so doctors can examine the sources behind them.

OpenEvidence’s small team began using Vercel to get early experiments online and kept that workflow as the product grew, relying on the platform to handle web deployments and capacity.

Copy link to headingBuilding software physicians depend on

The stakes are different when software helps inform medical decisions. An incorrect answer can affect how a doctor treats a patient, while an unavailable application can cut off access to evidence when it is needed.

OpenEvidence supported more than 20 million clinical consultations in January 2026. The company also reported that more than 100 million Americans were treated by doctors using OpenEvidence in 2025.

"Honestly, life or death is not inaccurate," says Kush Khosla, Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence. "We operate in situations where it's an ER and they really need to know what's going on. Uptime is very, very important to us."

"A lot of doctors and medical professionals are used to really outdated software," says Andy Yoon, Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence. A more modern experience still needs to meet physicians' expectations of speed, stability, clarity, and information they can trust. The small team needs a way to test updates to the web application before putting them into production and to roll back if something goes wrong.

Copy link to headingKeeping releases simple as the audience grows

Andy recalls why Vercel suited the team he joined at OpenEvidence. "I was pretty much the only engineer on our team coming from an actual frontend background," he says. "Most of our team works in Python and machine learning." He adds, "Given the makeup of our engineering team, Vercel really scaled with our needs so well."

The team builds its physician-facing web application with the Next.js framework. When engineers push changes to a development branch, Vercel builds and deploys a preview, giving them a link they can use for live demos and share with colleagues to try new features. Pushing or merging into the production branch then triggers the production build and deployment. If a release needs reverting, the team can roll back to a previous deployment.

That workflow lets the team release multiple times a day, with each change becoming available to a physician audience that Kush thinks about whenever he ships something:

If I push a frontend change, I know that 650,000 doctors will see that change in about five minutes. Vercel just takes it and deploys it to everybody. That sticks with me every single day whenever I'm pushing stuff.Kush Khosla Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence

Copy link to headingMore doctors without more provisioning

Keeping that application available means handling demand the team can’t always anticipate. Andy was scrolling through Slack when he saw the message that OpenEvidence had gone viral on TikTok, reaching around two million views in under a week. He watched traffic climb and checked the logs. Response times stayed fast and error rates remained near zero, and with no additional capacity to provision, he went back to his work.

Vercel has just completely scaled with that usage. We've never had it fall over due to capacity or had to provision anything extra. Just being able to trust that it's there, to the point where we don't really even think about it, is amazing.Andy Yoon Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence

Beyond sudden spikes, the team has accommodated sustained growth without rebuilding the web application.

"Not once have I had to think, now that we have five times as many doctors, what's happening to page loads or time to first paint," Kush says. "The scaling has happened so naturally that we end up focusing on other things."

Copy link to headingA 90% drop in serverless spend

As usage grew, VP of Engineering Micah Smith was watching compute costs. The team enabled Fluid compute for its functions on Vercel, and Micah described the result alongside the wider infrastructure budget:

"We reduced our serverless spend by 90% while maintaining the same performance, and even as we've scaled up to 1000x growth, Vercel is less than 5% of our overall infra spend."

Fluid compute lets multiple requests share a running function instance, so it can handle other work while a request waits for another service, such as a database or an AI backend, to respond. With Active CPU pricing, that waiting time doesn’t incur CPU charges, though memory remains billed while requests are in progress.

Copy link to headingA familiar workflow for a new audience

Take Home, OpenEvidence’s first patient-facing application, lets a doctor translate a clinical answer into plain language and share it with a patient, who logs in to review and save the evidence. Clinical-trial matching is also part of the application’s planned direction.

To support this expansion, the team uses a pattern established through dozens of early proofs of concept, each deployed as its own Vercel project with a custom domain. Stakeholders could open those applications and test the workflows for themselves. Getting new projects online in minutes helped the team find product-market fit and made it easier to win early enterprise partnerships.

Take Home has its own project and domain too, so engineers can update the patient experience without deploying the other applications.

We know Next and Vercel so well, we get these independent deployments that work seamlessly and are isolated from each other. There are all these other areas we want to move into, so let's just make that a new Vercel project.Kush Khosla Engineering Lead at OpenEvidence

With Take Home, evidence that helps a doctor during a consultation can become something a patient returns to afterward.

About OpenEvidence: OpenEvidence helps healthcare professionals find medical evidence at the point of care, with answers sourced, cited, and grounded in peer-reviewed literature. Physicians use it daily across more than 10,000 hospitals and medical centers in the United States. Its mission is to help doctors save lives and improve patient care. Learn more at openevidence.com.

It also reports active incidents from the Vercel status page.Each check reports OK, Warning, Failed, or Skipped. When vercel upgrade can't update the
entries.content:
Vercel CLI now includes 

vercel doctor
, which checks your setup and shows the command that fixes each problem it finds.

It checks the CLI version and install, your login and current team, the project link, and your project configuration in 

vercel.json
. It also reports active incidents from the Vercel status page.

Each check reports OK, Warning, Failed, or Skipped. When vercel upgrade can't update the installed CLI, the install check shows where the CLI runs from and how to reinstall it.

Doctor runs without a login or a linked project, and it never prompts, logs in, or links a project, so coding agents can run it before guessing at a fix. Add --json to get each check's status and suggested commands as structured output.

      
vercel doctor --json

CLI setup checks with JSON output

Update to the latest CLI version and run 

vercel doctor
to check your setup, or read the doctor command reference.

All of the same configuration properties are supported as in vercel.json, but it supports comments and has a flatter structure. All projects can now use vercel.toml. Use only one project configuration file: vercel.toml, vercel.json, or vercel.ts.For example, configuring Services:Read
entries.content:
Vercel now supports 

vercel.toml
, which allows you to to configure your project using the TOML configuration format. All of the same configuration properties are supported as in 
vercel.json
, but it supports comments and has a flatter structure.

All projects can now use 

vercel.toml
. Use only one project configuration file: vercel.toml, vercel.json, or vercel.ts.

For example, configuring Services:

vercel.toml

      
"$schema" = "https://openapi.vercel.sh/vercel.json"
# NextJS frontend[services.frontend]root = "frontend/"
# FastAPI backend[services.backend]root = "backend/"entrypoint = "main:app"
[[rewrites]]source = "/api/(.*)"destination = { service = "backend" }
[[rewrites]]source = "/(.*)"destination = { service = "frontend" }

Read the documentation.

entries.title: Vercel MCP now supports Client ID Metadata Documents
entries.summary: Any MCP client can now ask to connect to Vercel MCP. You still log in and approve each connection, but the client no longer has to be reviewed by Vercel first. Previously, Vercel reviewed and allowlisted each client and its redirect URIs by hand, and anything not on the list was rejected.To connect, a client publishes a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD), a JSON file on its own domain that describ
entries.content:
Any MCP client can now ask to connect to Vercel MCP. You still log in and approve each connection, but the client no longer has to be reviewed by Vercel first. Previously, Vercel reviewed and allowlisted each client and its redirect URIs by hand, and anything not on the list was rejected.

To connect, a client publishes a Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD), a JSON file on its own domain that describes it, and uses that file's HTTPS URL as its OAuth 

client_id
. This follows the MCP authorization spec, which now recommends CIMD over Dynamic Client Registration.

Because Vercel hasn't reviewed these clients, the consent screen shows where each one comes from: its name, its logo, and the hostname that serves its metadata document, for example "Claude Code by claude.ai". CIMD clients don't get the Vercel verified badge, so the hostname is what you're trusting when you approve.

Apps already registered with Vercel are unchanged.

Read the Vercel MCP documentation to connect your client.

entries.content:
Vercel MCP can now show your deployments as an interactive card inside ChatGPT and other chat clients that support MCP Apps.

The card shows live deployment status, build logs, and source and commit details, with a Visit button once the deployment URL is ready. You can send logs into the chat to debug with the model, or open the fullscreen view to read them beneath the card. For repositories linked to multiple projects, a project list lets you switch between them.

The card is Vercel MCP's first MCP App, built on the MCP Apps extension. Clients without app support receive the deployment state, preview URL, and commit as text instead. The 

open_deployments
tool looks up deployments by project, repository, or commit, with environment filtering. ChatGPT connects to Vercel MCP through its Connectors setup.

entries.content:
Flags Explorer is a tool in the Vercel Toolbar where you can see which feature flags are active on your end, and share them with your team, either by setting them for the branch or through a URL.

The Explorer surface has been redesigned to co-locate overrides, branch recommendations, and any related actions.

Whenever a branch has overrides set, they will be recommended to teammates visiting the deployment through a dialog.

Flags Explorer is available on all plans. Read the documentation to get started.
